title: Exchange maps of the Frobenius square
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a
prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in the chosen
algebraic closure $\Qlb$, an integer $n\geq1$, and a coefficient ring
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, with finite-level coefficient
category the finite-torsion constructible category
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility] and the integral, rational and
$\Qlb$ categories of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed],
[def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and
[def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a
separated finite-type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] morphism of
finite-type $k_0$-schemes, with base change $f:X\to Y$ to $k$, let
$g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$ and
$g_Y=\operatorname{id}_{Y_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$, $\gamma=\operatorname{Frob}_q$,
be the geometric Frobenii [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], and let
$\square_{f}=(f,f,g_Y,g_X,(g_X,f))$ be the Frobenius square of $f_0$, a
Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] by
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian]. Use the derived pullback
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the derived direct image
[def-weil-derived-direct-image], the extension by zero
[def-weil-extension-by-zero] and the compact-support direct image
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

1. *Direct-image exchange.* For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and
$K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$,

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K):Lg_Y^*Rf_*K\longrightarrow Rf_*Lg_X^*K
$$

is the ambient exchange transformation $\Ex^{A}_{\square_f}(K)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] for the coefficient sheaf
$R=(A_{E,n})$: the mate, under $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, of
$Lf^*Lg_Y^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_X^*Lf^*Rf_*K
\xrightarrow{Lg_X^*(\varepsilon_K)}Lg_X^*K$, whose first arrow is the
identification $\theta_{\square_f}$ of the square and $\varepsilon$ the
counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$ and
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K)$ is obtained from the
maps $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,m})$, $m\geq1$,
by the derived inverse limit, the rationalization and the common-stage
construction, in the same way as $Lg^*$ and $Rf_*$ themselves are obtained
from their finite levels.

2. *Compact-support exchange.* Choose a compactification
$X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}\overline X_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0$ of $f_0$ over $k_0$
[def-weil-compactifications-refinements], which exists by
[prop-compactification-refinement]. Its base change
$X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ to $k$ is a compactification
$c$ of $f$ ($j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper, both properties
being stable under base change). Put
$g_{\overline X}=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X_0}\times\Spec(\gamma)$. By
[lem-weil-frobenius-square-cartesian] for $p_0$, the square
$\square_p=(p,p,g_Y,g_{\overline X},(g_{\overline X},p))$ is Cartesian, and
by [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] for $j_0$ so is the square
$(j,j,g_{\overline X},g_X)$; let
$b_{g_{\overline X}}:Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!Lg_X^*$ be the
isomorphism of [lem-trf-open-square-exchange] for the latter square. For
$\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and $K$ in the domain of
[def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], with
$Rf_!K=Rp_*j_!K$ computed by $c$ (through the comparison isomorphism of
[prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] if $Rf_!$ was formed with
another compactification),

$$
 \operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}(K):Lg_Y^*Rp_*j_!K
 \xrightarrow{\ \operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}(j_!K)\ }
 Rp_*Lg_{\overline X}^*j_!K
 \xrightarrow{\ Rp_*(b_{g_{\overline X}}(K))\ }
 Rp_*j_!Lg_X^*K ,
$$

where $\operatorname{FrEx}_{p,*}$ is the direct-image exchange of item 1 for
$\square_p$. This is the compact-support exchange
$\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of [def-exchange-projection], whose recipe it follows,
for the Frobenius square. For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb$ and
$K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ it is obtained from the finite levels as in item 1.

Both $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,*}$ and $\operatorname{FrEx}_{f,!}$ are natural
transformations, being composites of natural transformations. The case used
for cohomology is $Y_0=\Spec k_0$, $f_0=a_{X_0}$, $f=a_X:X\to s=\Spec k$,
$g_Y=g_s=\Spec(\gamma)$, written $\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,*}$ and
$\operatorname{FrEx}_{X,!}$. That these maps are isomorphisms is not part of
this definition (part 2 of [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso]
for $f=a_X$).
